questions.text: For electrical rooms, which checked PEC rule family is most important to preserve?

options.text: Working space, headroom, illumination, and required access around equipment.
A decorative room name that replaces clear working space.
Storage shelves in front of service equipment.
Foreign ducts and piping placed freely above switchgear.

questions.rationale: The checked PEC family requires electrical working space, headroom, illumination, and related access clearances.
questions.code_citation: Article: Section Rooftop Equipment Areas (Cooling Tower, Exhaust Fan, Intake Louvers)

questions.text: Which coordination decision is source-safe for service equipment rooms?

options.text: Keep foreign pipes and ducts out of dedicated electrical equipment space where the PEC requires protection.
Use service-equipment rooms as general plumbing chases.
Let future maintenance access depend only on removable furniture.
Prioritize ceiling concealment over equipment clearances.

questions.rationale: The checked PEC family restricts foreign systems near service equipment and switchgear and requires coordinated working space.
questions.code_citation: Article: Section Space Allocation Rules of Thumb (Hospitality row); PD 1096 + ASHRAE hospitality standards

questions.text: Which mechanical-space planning idea is supported by the checked Salvan utilities family?

options.text: Plan for access, maintenance, ventilation, expansion, and noise control around utility equipment.
Use leftover space after architectural rooms are finalized.
Treat equipment rooms as storage rooms by default.
Avoid ventilation because mechanical rooms are not occupied.

questions.rationale: The checked Salvan family emphasizes access, maintenance, ventilation, expandability, and noise considerations for utility equipment spaces.
questions.code_citation: Article: Section Space Allocation Rules of Thumb (GFA percentage table for high-rise office)

questions.text: For HVAC plant rooms, which DOE energy-design principle is source-safe?

options.text: Size systems close to calculated loads and use controls or staging such as multiple chillers where appropriate.
Always oversize the plant without a load calculation.
Remove controls so all equipment runs continuously.
Ignore part-load operation in building systems.

questions.rationale: The checked DOE family addresses design loads, system sizing close to load, part-load strategies, multiple chiller units, controls, and VSDs.
